### 🔍 Key Changes with "Before-and-After" Contrasts

---

#### 1. **Scheduling Change: From July/August to June (2011–2018)**  
**Before 2011:**  
The tournament was played at the end of July or the beginning of August each year.  

**After 2011:**  
It moved to the first weekend in June (starting in 2012), and was played from Wednesday to Saturday to allow players more time to travel to the following week’s U.S. Open.  
➡️ *This shift aligned the event with the U.S. Open schedule, improving player logistics and visibility.*

> ✅ *Contrast emphasizes cause-effect: scheduling change due to U.S. Open proximity.*

---

#### 2. **Rebranding to Scandinavian Invitation (2019)**  
**Before 2019:**  
The event was known as the *Scandinavian Masters*, a men-only tournament on the European Tour.  

**After 2019:**  
Lagardère Group passed management to the European Tour, and the tournament was renamed the *Scandinavian Invitation*.  
➡️ *This marked a shift in ownership and branding, signaling a new era of management and possibly greater integration with the European Tour.*

> ✅ *Contrast highlights organizational change and rebranding.*

---

#### 3. **Launch of the Scandinavian Mixed (2020–2024)**  
**Before 2020:**  
The tournament was a men-only event (Scandinavian Masters/Invitation), with no female participation.  

**After 2020:**  
The European Tour and Ladies European Tour co-sanctioned the event as the *Scandinavian Mixed*, bringing 78 men and 78 women together to compete on the same course from different tees.  
➡️ *This was a historic first—equal prize money, shared rankings, and inclusion of women in a major men’s tour event.*  

> ✅ *Contrast emphasizes transformation from exclusion to inclusion, with structural and competitive innovation.*

> 📌 *Note: Despite the name change, the event was still held in June (originally scheduled), but was cancelled in 2020 due to the pandemic.*

---

#### 4. **Cancellation and Return (2020–2021)**  
**Before 2020:**  
The tournament was held annually in June (previously since 2012).  

**After 2020:**  
The event was **cancelled** due to the **COVID-19 pandemic**, like many other tournaments.  

**After 2021:**  
It **returned** in June 2021, with Jonathan Caldwell winning the inaugural mixed event.  
➡️ *This shows resilience and adaptation during a global crisis, with the event resuming after a one-year gap.*

> ✅ *Contrast highlights external disruption (pandemic) and recovery (return in 2021).*

---

#### 5. **Historic Women’s Victory and Event End (2022–2024)**  
**Before 2022:**  
Women competed in the Scandinavian Mixed, but had no chance to win on the European Tour.  

**After 2022:**  
Linn Grant became the **first woman to win on the European Tour** at the Scandinavian Mixed, winning by nine strokes.  
➡️ *This was a landmark moment in women’s golf, proving women could compete at the highest level in a men’s-style event.*

> ✅ *Contrast shows a shift from "token participation" to "pinnacle achievement."*

**After 2024:**  
Linn Grant won again in 2024, and the tournament was confirmed as **the final edition**.  
➡️ *The event concluded after a successful run of inclusion and excellence, ending in October 2024.*

> ✅ *Contrast shows the end of an era—after years of progress, the tournament was retired.*
